4.text: I mentioned before that the manner and customs of the clergy of the

5.text: Kolyma do not differ much from those of the other Russian creole population.

6.text: Not to speak of modern times, the Archives are full of historical indications to

7.text: that effect. I will cite only some of those that are connected with the mission.

8.text: Thus in 1821 the priest of Sredne-Kolymsk, Michael Sivtzov, was impeached

9.text: before the court because he took from a newly baptized Lamut his wedded

10.text: wife, and forced her to remain in his house. Many more accusations were added.

11.text: In 1826 the priest Basile Trifonov was impeached before the court on account

12.text: of his traffic in alcohol with the Chukchee. In 1837 the above-mentioned

13.text: chief official, Vinogradov, wrote a letter to the preacher of the Chukchee

14.text: mission of that time, saying that the said preacher had brought from the

15.text: Anui fair “a pile of Chukchee sins, to the amount of four pack-horses” (twenty-

16.text: four puds). The preacher answered, “This letter shows your lack of zeal for

17.text: the building-up of the church and for service to the fatherland.” The mission-

18.text: aries received funds and wares for presents to the Chukchee, and distributed

19.text: them in the same way as the civil authorities of the country. Thus each

20.text: newly baptized heathen received sugar, tobacco, and other things of value,

21.text: the same as when paying allegiance to the Czar. Both acts, however, usually

22.text: went together; and, as one of the missionaries writes in his report to the

23.text: bishop, “To be baptized for the heathen means to pay the tribute to the Czar

24.text: of heaven.” This method of encouraging people to be converted by bribing

25.text: them with presents led to many strange scenes. One of them is described

26.text: by Matushkin in “Wrangell’s Voyage.”¹ It happened at the Anui fair, where

27.text: a young Chukchee suddenly jumped out of the baptismal font and ran stark

28.text: naked around the room, crying, “Enough! I do not want any more of it!

30.text: It seems that sometimes the missionaries, even, were at the same time

31.text: the collectors of the tribute. Thus, in the year 1814 the before-mentioned

32.text: Gregory Slieptzov, when on his visit to the Chaun Chukchee, induced seventy-six

33.text: Chukchee men to take the oath of allegiance. Some of them were also

34.text: baptized. On this occasion he brought to Nishne-Kolymsk eighty-seven puds

35.text: of walrus-ivory and of various peltries; and all this he turned into the Treasury.²
